Why many products are banned in Europe

Well-known examples of substances that are permitted in the USA (with few exceptions) but strictly banned in the EU include: Titanium dioxide (E 171): A whitening agent widely used in the USA (e.g., in Skittles) but banned in the EU since 2022 due to suspected genotoxicity. Potassium bromate: A "dough conditioner" frequently used in US baked goods that is classified as carcinogenic and banned in the EU. Certain artificial colorants: Some dyes (such as Red 3 or Yellow 5) found in US sweets and beverages are no longer permitted for use in Europe. Storage and pesticide residues: US potatoes or fruits are often treated after harvest with chemical sprout inhibitors or preservatives that are not approved in Europe. Hormones and chlorine: The use of growth hormones in cattle farming (such as Ralgro) and the washing of poultry meat with chlorine for disinfection are also banned in the EU.
